sentences.text:
Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Ramesh Kumar Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
1. Heard ShriRamesh Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as Shri
Mvs Chauhan, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. This bail application has been filed seeking release of the accused/applicantPradeep Kumar on
bail, who is involved in Case Crime No. 81 of 2023 under Sections 376, 452, 504 & 506 I.P.C, Police
Station Dalmau, District Raebareli.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the First Information was lodged by the prosecutrix herself, mentioning therein that on 04.09.2022 at about 2 O'Clock in the night, the applicant came to her house, overpowered her and on the pretext of marriage, established physical relation with her.
It is further mentioned in the F.I.R, that after the said incident also, the applicant used to establish physical relation with the prosecutrix.

In the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C, she has stated that she is 32 years old lady and the mental condition of her Pradeep Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91705626/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: husband is not good, and on the pretext of marriage the applicant established physical relation with the prosecutrix many times, whereas, in the F.I.R, the prosecutrix has mentioned that she is a widow.
She has stated that her husband is mentally ill, therefore, the pretext of marriage plea taken by the prosecutrix is totally wrong.
Learned counsel for applicant further submitted that it is a case of consent and the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that the said incident took place on 04.09.2022 and the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C was filed on 28.10.2022, which is much belated and the First Information Report was lodged on 31.10.2023.
He further submitted that the medical report of the prosecutrix is not supporting the prosecution case.
He further stated that there is no previous criminal history of the applicant and he is languishing in jail since 03.05.2023.

5. Learned AGA has opposed the prayer of bail of the applicant and has submitted that as per the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C, it is a case of rape, therefore, bail of applicant is liable to be rejected.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, perusing the record, also considering the nature of allegations, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, the argument that it is a case of consent, the argument that there is change of version between the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C and the First Information Report, the argument that medical report of prosecutrix is not supporting the prosecution case, the argument that F.I.R has been lodged at a much belated stage, I find it to be a fit case for grant of bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Pradeep Kumar be released on bail in the above case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
